messages.text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

Thanks. What matters most to me is a fair financial share. I haven’t agreed to a discounted purchase, and I don’t want my share effectively subsidizing A. I’m not in a hurry, but I do want us to sort it out fairly.
I’d like to buy the house with my husband at a family discount. I want us to make it our home, but I know C’s agreement is needed, and she hasn’t agreed.
Thank you. I suppose I’d like to have some money to get a dance studio started. Dancing is my work, and having a place of my own would mean a lot. I’m not sure what’s fair or possible yet.
Mostly. I’d say: “C wants a fair financial share and has not agreed to subsidize A’s discounted purchase.” I’m not in a hurry.
That fits. The discount matters because I want to be financially independent; it isn’t mainly about feeling connected to the house.
Mostly, yes. I’d put it as: “B would like money to help her start a dance studio.” I don’t know what amount or timing is fair or possible.
The wording fits. An independent appraisal sounds reasonable as a starting point, but I’m not agreeing to a buyout yet. The value and terms need to be fair, with no discount subsidized by my share.
Entry 2 is okay. An appraisal doesn’t bother me, but it doesn’t mean I can afford the purchase without a family discount. I’m not sure the buyout or payment options would work legally or financially.
Upfront money would probably help, but I couldn’t say yes without knowing the appraisal and terms. I’m also not sure that a full third each is established, or that C is comfortable with a sale.
